cards.title: Change 'learn more' button to scroll to on-page contact form
cards.claim: For Influence Hunter, changing the 'learn more' button at the top of the site to automatically scroll down to the contact form on the same page (instead of linking to a separate contact page) was A/B tested and produced a 220% lift in conversions.
cards.action: Put the learn more button at the top of the site to automatically scroll down to the contact form itself on the same page instead of taking the user to a separate contact page.
applies_when: Landing page where users may not convert at the top and might convert further down
Users are clicking 'learn more' buttons throughout the page
Goal is to capitalize on interest while it is top of mind
unknowns: Sample size and statistical significance of the A/B test
Traffic source and audience for Influence Hunter
Whether the lift persists over time
Potential impact on user experience if the form is far down the page
evidence_quotes: what we AB tested was we put the learn more button at the top of the site to automatically scroll down to the contact form itself on the same page and we saw a 220% lift in conversions just from the ab test
initially what we had for their landing page was the learn more button would actually take the user to a separate contact page where they would then fill out the like an opt-in page

cards.title: Reduce contact form friction and improve clarity
cards.claim: The speaker recommends reducing friction on contact forms by combining first and last name into a full name field, keeping to four or fewer fields, separating placeholder and label, using a benefit-driven headline instead of 'Contact us', and adding bullet points, social proof, and next steps. These were among many changes for The Line Group that led to a 142% increase in conversions and qualified leads.
cards.action: Combine first and last name into a single full name field; keep the form to four fields or fewer; ensure form labels are not used as placeholders (separate placeholder and label); replace a generic 'Contact us' headline with a benefit-driven headline that communicates what the user will get; include three to four bullet points on what to expect after filling out the form, social proof at the point of form entry, and a short blurb about next steps.
applies_when: Contact form on a lead generation landing page
General audience with adequate traffic quality
Goal is to reduce friction and increase conversions
do_not_use_when: If traffic source is Facebook ads and gets a lot of unqualified traffic, additional layers of friction might be wanted
Depends on quality and volume of leads and capacity
unknowns: Exact contribution of each individual form change to the 142% increase
Whether four fields or fewer is optimal for all industries
Sample size and statistical significance for The Line Group results
evidence_quotes: first name and last name doesn't need to be two separate form entries this can just be combined into full name
try to keep it to four Forum fields or less

the form label is being used as a placeholder if I actually type in my email here and all of my other details what ends up happening is it actually removes what the label of the form field was in the first place
having contact us is redundant what I would want to see here is like a benefit driven headline as to what I can expect if I am to fill out the form

you also have these fundamentals of any High converting contact action which is three to four bullet points as to what I can expect if I fill out the form social proof at the point of form entry and then giving the user a short blurb as to what they can expect and next steps
this was one of the many changes that we made for the line group that led to a 140 2% increase in conversions and qualified leads

cards.title: Use progressive disclosure to simplify initial conversion action
cards.claim: Progressive disclosure means making the initial action simple (e.g., one email field) and then revealing more complex information or additional fields after the user takes the first step. The speaker cites Segment.com as an example where entering an email changes the form from one field to three.
cards.action: Start with a simple initial form field (e.g., work email) and progressively disclose additional fields after the user has taken that first step.
applies_when: Goal is to get more information from users while keeping conversion action simple
Users may be hesitant to fill out a long form initially
unknowns: Optimal number of additional fields to reveal
Potential for user annoyance or drop-off after first step
evidence_quotes: it's called Progressive disclosure so this is basically where you make the initial action simple you're kind of grabbing people in and making them feel like it's simple but then you're progressively disclosing more complex information

if you look at segment.com you can see right here at the very top of the website they have your work email and if I actually type in my email here what you can see is that it went from one form field to three
so it makes me feel like the action is simple all I need to do is enter my email to get a demo now that I've already entered my email I'm like okay I might as well go and complete everything else
